subject: Issue running SPDE model with group

messages.author: 03bc4090a2c2b3fb
messages.subject: Issue running SPDE model with group
parts:
Hello,

I am hoping someone might be able to help find a solution to this problem. I'm trying to run a spatio-temporal SPDE model where the SPDE is grouped by the number of years in the data, however every time I run this model, I get the attached error. The model does run when I remove the group (i.e., when it is a spatial-only model). My code is below. I would really appreciate any insight into where I am going wrong, as all the resources I have found indicate that this is the correct syntax for inla.spde.make.A() and inla.spde.make.index(). Thank you!

Kind regards,
Pascale

# Prepare the SPDE model
n_time <- length(unique(dat.cx$year))
time <- dat.cx$year - min(dat.cx$year) + 1
dat.cx$b0 <- 1 # intercept

spde1 <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh = mesh.gr, alpha = 2, constr = TRUE)

A1 <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh.gr, loc = cbind(dat.cx$longitude, dat.cx$latitude), group = time, n.group = n_time)

s.index <- inla.spde.make.index(name = "s", n.spde = spde1$n.spde, n.group = n_time)

vars <- names(dat.cx)[14:51]

# Prepare the data stack
stack.est <- inla.stack(tag = "est",
                        data = list(y = dat.cx$cx_pip, trap_nights = dat.cx$trap_nights),
                        A = list(1, 1, A1),
                        effects = list(dat.cx[, c("b0", vars)], # fixed effects
                                       list(week = dat.cx$week), # random effects
                                       s = s.index)) # spde

form0 <- y ~ 0 + b0 +
  f(s, model = spde1, group = s.group, control.group = list(model = "iid")) +
  f(week, model = "ar1")
mod0 <- inla(form0, offset = log(trap_nights),
             data = inla.stack.data(stack.est, spde = spde1),
             family = "nbinomial",
             control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE,
                                      A = inla.stack.A(stack.est)),
             control.compute = list(dic = TRUE),
             verbose = TRUE)
